artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan acting on the audit's 0-DELETE/14-KEEP verdict rather than deleting suites: a leaked-fixture reaper pass in claude-refresh.sh plus a live backlog sweep, suppression of verify-deploy.sh's fixed corpus probe on gate-narrowed invocations (measured live at 2.2-2.4s of a 4.07s minimal invocation, paid 26-29 times by each of the two most expensive suites), regeneration of both stale probe artifacts against the optimized system, and a specs/decisions/ verdict record carrying the KEEP roster, the four-way suite-population counting methodology, and the demotion-tier non-recommendation.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh ends every invocation with a 'standing corpus-size probe' that shells out to script-inventory.sh --size-line. Measured live 2026-11-17: 2.37s against the repo root and 2.22s against a non-git rsync copy of agent-system/extensions/, out of 4.07s total for `verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 1` -- i.e. ~58% of a minimal gate-narrowed invocation, and it fires in BOTH fixture shapes test suites build, because script-inventory.sh falls back to a filesystem walk when `git ls-files` finds nothing. Any suite that invokes verify-deploy.sh many times with --only-gate (cache-equivalence: 29 static run_vd call sites; the crash-net suite: one invocation per registered gate id) therefore pays this fixed cost per invocation, and its wall clock is dominated by invocation_count x fixed_overhead rather than by the gates it names. The probe's guard is `[ -d $TARGET/agent-system/extensions ] && [ -f $TARGET/.../script-inventory.sh ]`, so a deploy-consumer-shaped fixture with no agent-system/extensions directory never pays it -- which is why the cheapest verify-deploy-touching suites are the ones whose fixtures lack that directory.
